correctness.rationale: An inverse-monoid congruence on free monogenic Munn intervals that identifies distinct elements must identify distinct idempotents: the range and domain intervals uniquely determine the triple. Meeting with a large opposite idempotent and conjugating by a sufficiently long power yields uniform eventual periodicity of at least one interval extent. Reducing this extent leaves O(1) choices for each terminal displacement and other extent; both have O(n) options in a word ball. Cubic source growth and the bicyclic quadratic sharpness follow from exact normal-form length and unique reduced words. The standalone checker independently tests finite cases but is not an infinite proof.
